 Credit: Far Out / Alamy / Eva Rinaldi The actor Jim Carrey and Robin Williams both called the greatest of all time: “I definitely was affected”
 Scott Campbell October 29th, 2026 · 8:15pm GMT Follow us on Google Discover Even though they were separated by a generation, Jim Carrey and Robin Williams were both massively influenced by the same actor, and it’s not hard to tell.
 Both of them got their start on the stand-up circuit before graduating to first television and then cinema, but they both achieved stardom in different ways. They’ve got a lot in common, but it wouldn’t be fair or accurate to even suggest that Carrey and Williams had identical rises to the top.
 For one thing, the former almost entirely abandoned live comedy in favour of acting, and his breakthrough role on the small screen as a cast member on In Living Color wasn’t a showcase built entirely around him, but he was clearly talented enough to stand out among a crowded pack.
 Williams never gave up on stand-up, although it became more infrequent once he became a household name, whereas his big break in front of a televised audience, Mork & Mindy , was built entirely around him . Once he outgrew the confines of the sitcom, though, it took him a while to reach the next level.
 By contrast, it didn’t take Carrey very long at all, relatively speaking. By the start of 1994, he’d played the leading role in one feature, which was released a decade earlier. By the end of the year, he’d taken top billing in three of them, all of which became massive hits and catapulted him onto the A-list.
 As for Williams, it wasn’t until Good Morning, Vietnam and the Academy Award nomination that came with it, in what was his seventh big-screen lead, that he finally gained recognition as a movie star. Obviously, as two of the biggest comedy stars of their respective eras, there are plenty of similarities, including their lifelong adoration for Peter Sellers.
 The Oscar-winning Good Will Hunting alum considers Dr Strangelove not only the greatest comedy ever made, but the film that had the biggest impact on his entire life. Who did he call the best actor never to win an Oscar of their own? Sellers, of course, and his fondness for the multi-talented and often very difficult performer was evident in many of his own performances.

 In 1968, Christopher Lee made a movie he was never happy with. Decades later, he wanted a remake with CGI 
 Which picture had the biggest impact on a young Carrey when he was growing up and dreaming of making people laugh for a living? A Shot in the Dark , starring Sellers . The rubber-faced Canadian noted, not that he had to, that he “definitely was affected” by the Pink Panther headliner, but he didn’t want to earn the same reputation for being a nightmare behind the scenes, which he sort of did eventually on Man in the Moon .
 Two of modern Hollywood’s most famous and successful comic actors naming one of the industry’s most naturally gifted comic actors as the best they’d ever seen may not be revelatory, but it just goes to show how deeply Sellers managed to sink his influential and inimitable claws into an entire genre, and they’re far from the only ones who feel that way.
